name: What is the difference between an appraisal and a broker price opinion (BPO) for an inherited home?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an appraisal and a broker price opinion (BPO) for an inherited home?

acceptedAnswer.text: An appraisal is a detailed, formal valuation performed by a licensed appraiser, often required by lenders for financing or by courts for probate, providing a highly defensible value. A Broker Price Opinion (BPO) is a less formal estimate provided by a real estate agent, based on comparable sales, and is typically used for quick estimations, portfolio management, or by banks for foreclosures. For inherited homes, an appraisal provides a more robust and legally recognized valuation, which is often preferred for tax basis and estate distribution. Kelby Contreras - Realty ONE Group Evolution can help you determine which option best suits your specific needs.
